newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada paper chides government on proposed MMT ban.
newsitem.headline: Canada paper chides government on proposed MMT ban.

text.p: A leading business newspaper, the Financial Post, chided the federal government on Friday for its strategy in trying to ban the fuel additive MMT.

Environment Minister Sergio Marchi made it clear this week that he intends to go ahead with a bill to ban the import and interprovincial trade in MMT, produced in the United States by Ethyl Corp and imported by its subsidiary Ethyl Canada.
The Financial Post's lead editorial said the government should have launched an independent study on whether the additive gums of cars' emission systems as automobile manufacturers claim.

And it said that if the real concern was environmental damage, then it should have banned it outright under the Canadian Environmental Protection Act, rather than trying to erect a trade barrier which Ethyl is now challenging with a US$200 million claim against the Canadian government.
The bill is at its final stage in Parliament, which returns from its summer recess next week, but how fast it advances will depend on the priorities set by the cabinet.
